Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What is considered the essential requirement for all entrepreneurs?

options.D: taking risks

questions.questionText: A new section of a road is provided toll-free by the government. What best describes this good?

options.D: a public good

questions.questionText: Eastern European nations have changed from planned to market economies. Which policy was least likely to have been adopted?

options.D: permitting changes in the money supply

questions.questionText: Rice and pasta are both basic foods in a country. How would a health scare concerning rice affect the market for pasta?

options.A: There will be a shift of demand and a contraction of supply.
options.B: There will be a shift of demand and an extension of supply.
options.C: There will be a shift of supply and a contraction of demand.
options.D: There will be a shift of supply and an extension of demand.

questions.questionText: Some goods are over-consumed in a market economy. What is likely to be the cause of this?

options.B: Consumers undervalue the benefits of consuming the goods.
options.C: There is excess supply in the market for the goods.
options.D: There is imperfect information in the market.

questions.questionText: A family is willing to pay a maximum of $600, $500 and $400 for air tickets for the mother, father and daughter to attend a wedding in another city. The airline announces a promotional air fare of $450 per ticket, provided at least three tickets are purchased. What will be the consumer surplus gained by the family if they use the promotional offer?
After a 10% decrease in a consumer’s income, the consumer’s demand for a good rises from 100 to 105. What is the value of the consumer’s income elasticity of demand for this good?

In 2010, poor harvests reduced fruit crops and furniture producers gave big discounts on furniture products. How might these changes have affected the position of the supply curve for the products? fruit furniture producers

options.A: no change shift to the left
options.B: shift to the left no change
options.C: shift to the left shift to the left
options.D: shift to the right no change

questions.questionText: In the diagram, D and S represent the demand for and supply of smartphones. Many components used in the production of smartphones are imported. The initial equilibrium is at point X. The exchange rate has depreciated at the same time as the price of a complementary good decreased. Which point in the diagram could represent the new equilibrium? S S price S B

options.A: X D C D D D O quantity

questions.questionText: The diagrams show the demand for and the supply of houses. In the short run, the stock of houses for sale, S , is fixed. A government decides to allow some agricultural land to be used for building houses and subsidises lower-income buyers of the new houses. Which diagram shows the long-run situation?

The equation for the quantity demanded, Q , for a product is D Q = 400 – 20P D where P = price in $. The quantity supplied, Q , is given by Q = 100 + 40P. S S Which change will occur if the price rises from $5 to $6?

options.A: The market will move from equilibrium to shortage.
options.B: The market will move from equilibrium to surplus.
options.C: The market will move from shortage to surplus.
options.D: The market will move from surplus to shortage.

questions.questionText: What is the most likely cause of the continuous increase in prices of famous paintings by now dead artists?

options.A: the increasing technological ability to copy famous paintings perfectly
options.B: the popular view that famous paintings are an appreciating asset
options.C: the totally inelastic supply of famous paintings by dead artists
options.D: the wish of governments to treat art galleries as merit goods

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be regressive?

options.D: unemployment benefits

questions.questionText: What is necessary for an action to be classed as a transfer payment?

options.A: It must include a cash payment.
options.B: It must involve a banking transaction.
options.C: It must originate from government activity.
options.D: It must relate to a non-productive activity.

questions.questionText: The government imposes a specific indirect tax of $1 on each unit of a good sold. How does the imposition of the tax shift the demand or supply curve of the good?

options.A: The demand curve of the good will shift vertically downwards by $1.
options.B: The demand curve of the good will shift vertically upwards by $1.
options.C: The supply curve of the good will shift vertically downwards by $1.
options.D: The supply curve of the good will shift vertically upwards by $1.

questions.questionText: Which term relates to a fall in the domestic real value of a currency?

options.D: inflation

questions.questionText: What must be the result for a country of a rise in its export prices relative to its import prices?

options.A: a deficit in its trade in goods
options.B: an improvement in its terms of trade
options.C: an increase in its inflation rate
options.D: a rise in its exchange rate

questions.questionText: Country X can produce a product at a lower opportunity cost than country Y. Which term best describes this statement?

options.D: terms of trade

questions.questionText: For a given year, economy X publishes the following. $bn Gross Domestic Product (GDP) 100 factor income earned by residents of 10 economy X working in foreign countries factor income earned in 25 economy X by non-residents What is the size of the Gross National Income (GNI) for country X?
Which combination is possible for an economy experiencing zero inflation? average average nominal wages real wages

options.D: unchanging rising

questions.questionText: The graph shows the rate of inflation in Japan from April 2020 to February 2021. 0.4 0.3 0.2 inflation 0.2 0.1 0.1 0.1 rate 0 –0.2 –0.4 –0.4 –0.4 –0.6 –0.6 –0.8 –1 –0.9 –1.2 –1.2 Apr May June July Aug Sept Oct Nov Dec Jan Feb 2020 2021 Over which period did disinflation occur in Japan?

options.D: October 2020 to February 2021

questions.questionText: The diagram shows three production possibility curves (PPC) for a country, labelled 3, 2 and 1. The original PPC for the country is 2. This country experiences a fall in its working population and then this is followed by a long period of recession. consumer goods s t u r
A government increases the rate of income tax. What is the effect, in the short run, on the aggregate demand curve or the aggregate supply curve?

options.A: The aggregate demand curve shifts left.
options.B: The aggregate demand curve shifts right.
options.C: The aggregate supply curve shifts left.
options.D: The aggregate supply curve shifts right.

questions.questionText: A country’s current account deficit is larger this year than last. What is the most likely reason for this increase?

options.A: Demand for domestically produced goods has risen.
options.B: Domestic inflation has risen faster than the inflation of its major trading partners.
options.D: The exchange rate has depreciated.

questions.questionText: Which supply-side measure is most likely to produce short-run growth in a country’s aggregate supply?

options.A: easing of controls on immigration of workers
options.D: privatisation of public utilities

questions.questionText: Which tax may a government use to reduce inequality?

options.D: specific indirect tax

questions.questionText: A foreign government pays a UK university to educate its students. How would this be recorded on the balance of payments current account of the UK? current account money flows component

options.D: trade in services outflow

questions.questionText: A government wants to reduce inflation. It has decided to cut government spending by $1bn. The diagram shows different starting positions for the country’s aggregate demand (AD) curve. AS price level AD AD AD AD O real GDP Which starting position for the aggregate demand curve would make this policy least effective?

options.A: AD B AD C AD D AD

questions.questionText: A government reduces the rate of tax firms are charged on their land and buildings. How is this likely to affect the economy’s price level and real output? price level real output
